On Thu, Jul 23, 2026 at 11:38 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Tom — looping Rishi and Grace to draft the crosswalk.

Tom —

Attached is a first-pass workbook (Hosted_vs_Dedicated_vs_Private_Detail.xlsx) with:
- Tab 1: Hosted baseline rates (per 1k tokens where applicable), assumptions (model sizes, avg tokens/req).
- Tab 2: Dedicated reserved cost model (monthly reserved pool cost, effective $/token at different utilization points, autoscale burst pricing).
- Tab 3: Private/on-prem (one-time platform license, estimated infra OPEX + capital depreciation placeholder, optional managed services add-on).
- Tab 4: Scenario math for the three usage profiles you requested.

High-level differences to call out:
- Hosted: variable cost dominates; good for low-to-moderate volume and spike-friendly use. No infra ownership. Per-token baseline includes model compute + runtime optimizations + shared KV cache hit assumptions (we assume 10% prefix cache hit by default in the hosted baseline).
- Dedicated: shifts to a hybrid model — monthly reserved pool (fixed) + small incremental per-token or burst premium. Effective unit cost falls as utilization increases. Dedicated includes dedicated KV cache capacity for your tenant which raises cache hit rates in practice (we used +15% hit in scenarios).
- Private (on-prem): heavy upfront license and onboarding fees, plus your infra CAPEX/OPEX. Unit cost can be lowest at very high predictable utilization but you absorb hardware refresh and HW ops. Also note private deployments often exclude cloud egress line items but add network/security integration costs.

Key assumptions we used in the workbook (editable):
- Model: quantized 8-bit variant for cost math (if you want fp16, switch multiplier ~1.6x to account for higher compute).
- Cache behavior: hosted shared prefix cache 10% hit; dedicated tenant cache +15% absolute; private assumed CDN/local cache 20% hit.
- Support: standard included SLA for hosted; dedicated includes premium support at additional 10% of reserved cost; private support typically quoted as a % of license or a per-seat managed services fee.
- Setup: Dedicated: one-time provisioning & validation fee (one week effort). Private: larger on-prem onboarding + optional 90-day managed transition.

Sample numbers from the draft (rounded, list for CFO):
- Hosted baseline: $0.00060 / token (2k token request => $1.20 per request at baseline).
- Dedicated reserved: $45,000 / month reserved pool (example) => at 60% utilization gives ~$0.00028 / token effective. Burst allowances billed at a premium or consumed from reserved buffer.
- Private: License + onboarding $500k one-time + infra estimate $X/mo (varies by cluster size) => at steady-state 200M tokens/month can be ~$0.00018 / token (depends heavily on amortization).

I'll be at the 30-minute walkthrough times Vanessa proposed; I can also present the spreadsheet line-by-line. Let me know whether you want the draft numbers moved to a formal quote with line items for legal/procurement.

--

Thanks for the detailed draft — appreciate the clear assumptions. A few procurement/CFO clarifications before we take this to legal: 

1) Cache/KV: please confirm how you attribute costs when tenant has high cache hit rates. If Arena observes 25% prefix cache hit in production, how does that reduce our committed reserved sizing and price?
2) Quantization: we need firm guidance on model parity for LLM-1-large-q8a vs fp16 LLM-1-large. If quantized is not fully parity, CFO wants to see quality delta risk line item (we may accept a performance SLA discount).
3) Autoscale bursts: can you cap monthly overage charges; procurement prefers a soft cap with negotiated burst buckets rather than open-ended per-token overage.
4) Discounting: Arena is evaluating a 12-month committed plan across production and non-prod. We would like to request a 20% discount off the baseline hosted per-token and a committed reserved discount schedule for Dedicated. Please include a worked example.

Please add a single-sheet summary formatted for our CFO (line items: one-time fees, recurring reserved, per-token, support, estimated monthly total under S1/S2/S3). After that we'll route to legal for MSAs and to finance for payment terms.

procurement team
Arena AI

Thanks — attached is a consolidated CFO-friendly summary and an updated ratecard (Redwood_Ratecard_Q3_v2.xlsx) plus a Dedicated PO template for your procurement docs (Dedicated_PO_Template.pdf). Highlights below (see attached sheet "CFO_Summary"):

Summary / proposed commercial outline (ARENA-2026-07):
- Baseline hosted (assumption: LLM-1-large-q8a): $0.00060/token list.
- One-time onboarding & validation: $8,500 (applies to both Hosted & Dedicated; Private onboarding scoped separately).
- Dedicated: tiered reserved pricing: 6-month commit $40,000/mo equivalent pool (example) => effective unit ~ $0.00030/token at 60% util; 12-month commit gets additional 8% discount on reserved fee.
- Private (on-prem): example license + onboarding $475,000 one-time + estimated infra O&M $12k/mo for the smaller cluster profile. Exact numbers will require infra sizing workshop.
- Discounts: we can offer a blended approach for your 12-month commitment: 15% off hosted per-token plus a committed-reserved discount schedule for Dedicated (we can bridge to 20% total effective discount at 12-month firm commit + prepay). Final discount depends on committed volume and payment terms.
- Burst protection: we will include a negotiated burst bucket (example: 20% of monthly committed tokens) with an overage cap and predefined top-up rates — we will include an example in the formal quote.
- Cache sensitivity: if Arena demonstrates 25% measured prefix cache hit, the Dedicated reserved sizing model reduces required reserved vCPU/GPU by ~12-18% in our scenario sheet (we've included an "adjusted sizing" column in CFO_Summary).
- Quantization: LLM-1-large-q8a is used in these scenarios. We can provide an A/B eval run (3–5 day sample) to measure any accuracy delta; if a material quality delta is identified we will propose a remediation credit structure.

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-minute CFO/finance walkthrough for 07/06 and 07/08 PDT (please confirm availability).
- If you confirm intent to proceed with a 12-month firm commit, we'll prepare a formal quote and a DocuSign proposal (link below) with the reserved pricing and burst cap terms.
